thread:
lee: Quick sync — drafting Q3 runtime perf OKRs and need to lock initiative order. I sketched three bets: (A) kernel fusion improvements for Llama-family, (B) adaptive quant pipeline + validation harness, (C) KV-prefetch + prefix cache eviction tuning. Which order gives best customer impact vs delivery risk?

maria: short take: customers hitting p95 latency regressions care most about C then A. quant (B) is high ROI but risky in testing.

ajay: can we split B into B1 (offline quant profiles + tests) and B2 (online adaptive)? B1 looks low-risk and quick.

sam: agree w/ ajay. propose priority: C -> A -> B1 -> B2. C is operational and unblocks most enterprise customers.

ciara: we need launch criteria per initiative. For C (KV-prefetch), I suggest: 1) p95 latency improvement >= 8% on long-tail workloads, 2) no increase in error-rate, 3) Canary pass on Dedicated pool for 48h.

lee: +1 for concrete criteria. Add SLO guardrail: token-cost delta <= 3% for inference. Some prefetch strategies inflate tokens due to padding.

perf-bot: Canary check template created: \n```\ncanary_config:\n  duration: 48h\n  sample_ratio: 5%\n  metrics:\n    - name: p95_latency\n      threshold: -8% # relative improvement\n    - name: error_rate\n      threshold: 0% # no regression allowed\n    - name: token_cost\n      threshold: 3% # relative increase allowed\n```\n
maria: for A (kernel fusion) launch criteria: 1) end-to-end latency reduction on small-batch chat workloads >= 12%, 2) peak throughput >= current baseline on 8k context, 3) perf regression tests across fp16/4bit-quant pass.

ajay: raising a tradeoff: fusion increases codepath complexity and may block M1/M2 mac builds. We should consider a phased rollout: server-only first, then edge.

sam: also flagged: CI flakiness on quant tests last sprint. If we push B2 before stabilizing harness we risk rollbacks. B1 must include deterministic eval artifacts and a regression suite.

ciara: customer asks backlog: two enterprise customers requested strict tail-latency SLA in EMEA. They will accept dedicated routing only if we can demonstrate KV-prefetch and fallback policies. This pushes C up in business impact scoring.

lee: Proposal for prioritization rubric (simple): Business impact (0-5), Risk (0-5 low better), Dev effort (0-5), Observability cost (0-5). Score = impact - risk - effort - obs_cost. Quick calc: C=5-2-2-1=0? hmm math but relative ordering remains.

maria: can we attach rough engineering weeks so PM/planning can schedule? My estimates: C: 6w (tuning+canary infra), A: 8w, B1: 3w, B2: 6w.

ajay: dependency note: A requires new kernel selection hooks in runtime scheduler. That touches routing logic (small change) but needs perf e2e. Add a TODO to spec.

lee: Action items: \n- ciara: draft customer-facing canary playbook for C and capture acceptance language (due Tue)\n- ajay: scope B1 and create deterministic quant harness PR with baseline artifacts (due Fri)\n- maria: update roadmap spreadsheet w/ weeks and relative priority (due Mon)\n- sam: add canary dashboards and retention for 7d (due Wed)\n
ciara: noted. I'll ping Legal for SLA wording once playbook done.

maria: +emoji: :thumbsup:

lee: thanks — we'll reconvene Thurs 10am for final OKR commitments. If anyone sees a big blocker, flag here before EOD.

perf-bot: Reminder: perf-budget budget owner tag @maria will be notified for any canary failures.
